Mindmap · How does V2 work?

Start at the center and follow the four branches. Expand any node for the action, its meaning for real estate and the supporting transaction. This map explains the completed BNB Smart Chain Testnet rehearsal.

Expand a node for its explanationTransaction links provide evidence
One property · One record · One cash flowORI-PILOT-01 · 1,000 shares · Wallets A and B

  1. 1 · Property recordWhich property and valuation?

    Create an on-chain property recordOne property ID, one rehearsal contract

    On-chain actionA deploys a contract with a fixed synthetic property ID. Its address identifies this property’s share ledger, state and rental payouts.

    Meaning for the projectA real deployment must connect this record to a verified property, its owner and the real-world legal structure.

    constructor(propertyId)
    Transaction 1 ↗
    Record and renew valuation evidenceA document fingerprint with an expiry

    On-chain actionA records a valuation file’s SHA-256 digest and expiry. Re-hashing an unchanged file gives the same fingerprint. Share transfers require a valid pricing record.

    Meaning for the projectValuation research and approval happen off-chain. This function records evidence and expiry. Sale prices and rent still require appropriate data sources.

    setPrice(digest, validUntil)
    Transaction 1 ↗ Transaction 2 ↗

  2. 2 · Share ownershipWho holds how many shares?

    Issue 1,000 shares to ACreate smaller participation units

    On-chain actionA issues once, crediting 1,000 shares to A’s contract ledger balance. The contract checks operator authority, pricing validity and pause status.

    Meaning for the projectOne property is divided into smaller units to explore small-ticket participation. V2 uses an internal contract balance ledger. Legal rights require a real-world structure.

    issue(firstHolder)
    Transaction 1 ↗
    Transfer 400 shares to BA retains 600, B holds 400

    On-chain actionA signs the transfer to B. The contract debits A, credits B and checkpoints the shares multiplied by time accumulated before the transfer.

    Meaning for the projectChanging holders changes future rental accrual from the transfer time. This run transfers shares. A paid purchase flow is still future work.

    transferShares(B, 400)
    Transaction 1 ↗

  3. 3 · SafeguardsWhen should actions be blocked?

    Revoke the pricing recordBlock transfers with invalid pricing

    On-chain actionA revokes pricing by setting its expiry to the current timestamp. Further transfers encounter PriceExpired until A records valid pricing again.

    Meaning for the projectWhen pricing evidence needs review, the platform can block transfers while addressing the data. Previously earned rent remains recorded.

    revokePrice()
    Transaction 1 ↗
    Pause during an incidentTemporarily halt sensitive actions

    On-chain actionA sets paused to true. In V2, issuance, transfers, closing, funding and rent claims are blocked with Paused.

    Meaning for the projectThe operator gains an incident-response control. Detecting manipulation or attacks and deciding when to pause require external monitoring procedures.

    setPaused(true)
    Transaction 1 ↗
    Resume operationsContinue after incident handling

    On-chain actionA sets paused to false. Subsequent actions still need their own conditions, such as valid pricing, a closed period or full funding.

    Meaning for the projectResuming requires an authorized decision. Share balances and recorded rental rights survive the pause.

    setPaused(false)
    Transaction 1 ↗
    Check rejected actionsRead and simulate with eth_call

    On-chain actionRead-only calls simulate transfers with revoked pricing or a paused contract. They return an expected error without broadcasting a transaction or paying gas.

    Meaning for the projectRead-only calls help check conditions before signing. The historical Paused error was replayed. The RPC returned missing trie node for the historical pricing-revocation block. The JSON record preserves this limit.

    eth_call → PriceExpired / Paused
    Read-only check results JSON

  4. 4 · Rental cash flowWho earns rent, and how much?

    Explicitly close the rental periodFix the cutoff for rental accrual

    On-chain actionA signs the close. The contract stores the ending timestamp and stops share transfers in this single-period rehearsal.

    Meaning for the projectA clear cutoff supports allocation by holding time. V2 closes when A requests it, with no preset 20-minute deadline.

    closePeriod()
    Transaction 1 ↗
    Fund the rental poolFunds must arrive before payout

    On-chain actionA sends a total of 6,000,000 wei tBNB into the contract. Funding can be partial. Claims require the full rehearsal pool.

    Meaning for the projectA real deployment needs a manager to collect rent, reconcile costs and confirm distributable funds before funding the pool.

    fund() payable
    Transaction 1 ↗
    A and B claim their earned rentAllocate by shares × holding time

    On-chain actionEach wallet signs its own claim. The contract calculates rent, marks it claimed and transfers tBNB. A received 4,352,203 wei and B received 1,647,796 wei.

    Meaning for the projectSomeone transferring some or all shares retains rent accrued earlier. Rental allocation depends on holding history as well as the closing share balance.

    claim()
    Transaction 1 ↗ Transaction 2 ↗
    Reject a second claimEach wallet claims once per period

    On-chain actionAfter settlement, claimed(A) and claimed(B) are true. Repeating either claim through eth_call returns DuplicateClaim.

    Meaning for the projectThis prevents paying the same rental entitlement twice. Total payouts were 5,999,999 wei, leaving 1 wei of rounding remainder in this prototype.

    claimed(holder) / DuplicateClaim
    Read-only check results JSON

Rehearsal reconciled

A holds 600 shares and B holds 400. Both received rent and were blocked from claiming twice. The pool retains a 1 wei rounding remainder.

See the settlement and all 11 operation transactions ↗
Why did A receive more than 60% of the rent with 600 closing shares?

Rent = pool × accumulated (shares × holding time) / (1,000 × period duration).

The actual period lasted 1,021 seconds. A held all 1,000 shares for the first 320 seconds, then transferred 400 to B for the remaining 701 seconds.

WalletHolding historyPaid
A1,000 shares × 320 seconds + 600 shares × 701 seconds4,352,203 wei
B400 shares × 701 seconds1,647,796 wei
Three execution layers and what this run demonstrates

Real-world layer verifies the unit, owner, legal records, valuation and actual rent collected.

Attestation layer authorized parties sign data and approve actions. In V2, A deploys, updates pricing and controls pausing.

Contract layer checks permissions and conditions, records shares and holding time, blocks actions and pays the funded pool according to its programmed rules.

V2 uses one synthetic asset, one rental period and test tBNB. Linking real property rights, approved valuations, actual rental receipts and guarantors requires later implementation. Vinhomes Grand Park is an independent research case study.

Reading this map requires no wallet connection. Evidence links expose the public records of the V2 run.

V2 completed on BSC Testnet

Issued 1,000 synthetic shares, transferred 400 from A to B, explicitly closed the period, funded rent and paid both holders. Both duplicate claims reverted with DuplicateClaim in read-only calls.

The 1,021-second period closed 701 seconds after the transfer. Payments match each wallet’s shares multiplied by holding time. These are testnet payouts.

The 1 wei rounding remainder remains in this single-period prototype. Price revocation and pause/resume events are listed below. Safeguards are controlled by the operator. The underlying property record is synthetic.
